80579210268b61ff389629fd202a0b1ca0b79eb7.summary: A December 2022 article reports that South Korean officials said hackers believed to be operating from North Korea breached the internal network of KAERI, a government nuclear research organisation, through a VPN server vulnerability. Thirteen IP addresses abused the flaw, and one was linked to infrastructure used by Kimsuky. KAERI first denied the intrusion, then apologised. The article also cites a Kimsuky spear-phishing campaign against South Korean government entities, and a 2019 US Treasury sanction of Lazarus, Andariel and Bluenoroff.

The page indexes many vendor and research reports, from 2014 to 2025, on SmokeLoader campaigns, loaders and related malware. Listed items include activity against Ukrainian and Taiwanese targets, a CVE exploited in a zero-day campaign, and a 2025 Operation Endgame follow-up with five detentions.

809d2511cc72fc1d1433cc2fa5d9736013637b33.summary: Analysis of RokRat, a remote access Trojan that the report says is primarily used by the North Korean state-sponsored group APT37, also known as ScarCruft. Infection starts with phishing emails carrying ZIP files with hidden LNK shortcuts, which run a multi-stage PowerShell and batch chain to decrypt and load the payload in memory. RokRat profiles the host, captures screenshots and lists processes. It uses the cloud services pCloud, Yandex and Dropbox as command-and-control channels and includes anti-analysis checks. It can run commands, scan drives, collect files and download further…
